fr.title: Augmentation de salaire au 1er janvier : quels États et villes augmentent le salaire minimum pour 2027

segments.src: Every year, millions of American workers see a slightly bigger paycheck on the first day of January, and they do not have to ask for it.
segments.tr: Chaque année, des millions de travailleurs américains constatent un chèque de paie légèrement plus important le premier jour de janvier, et ils n'ont pas à le demander.

segments.src: In a growing number of states and cities, the minimum wage rises automatically at the start of the year.
segments.tr: Dans un nombre croissant d'États et de villes, le salaire minimum augmente automatiquement au début de l'année.

segments.src: Here is how those increases work, where they tend to happen, and what they mean for workers and small employers.
segments.tr: Voici comment fonctionnent ces augmentations, où elles ont tendance à se produire, et ce qu'elles signifient pour les travailleurs et les petits employeurs.

segments.src: *Note: Exact 2027 rates are typically announced by state agencies in the fall.
segments.tr: *Remarque : Les taux exacts pour 2027 sont généralement annoncés par les agences étatiques à l'automne.

segments.src: Always confirm the final figure with your state or city labor department before making payroll or budgeting decisions.*
segments.tr: Confirmez toujours le chiffre final auprès du département du travail de votre État ou de votre ville avant de prendre des décisions en matière de paie ou de budget.*

segments.src: ## Why do so many wages change on January 1?
segments.tr: ## Pourquoi tant de salaires changent-ils le 1er janvier ?

segments.src: The federal minimum wage has been $7.25 an hour since 2009, and Congress has not changed it since.
segments.tr: Le salaire minimum fédéral est de $7.25 de l'heure depuis 2009, et le Congrès ne l'a pas modifié depuis.

segments.src: Because of that, much of the action has moved to the states and local governments.
segments.tr: De ce fait, une grande partie de l'action s'est déplacée vers les États et les gouvernements locaux.

segments.src: Roughly thirty states and the District of Columbia set a minimum above the federal level, and many of them have built automatic adjustments into law so that lawmakers do not need to vote every year.
segments.tr: Environ trente États et le district de Columbia fixent un minimum supérieur au niveau fédéral, et nombre d'entre eux ont intégré des ajustements automatiques dans la loi afin que les législateurs n'aient pas à voter chaque année.

segments.src: There are two common approaches:
segments.tr: Il existe deux approches courantes :

segments.src: - **Scheduled step increases.** A law sets a path, such as a series of fixed raises over several years until a target (often $15 or more) is reached.
segments.tr: - **Augmentations progressives prévues.** Une loi fixe une trajectoire, telle qu'une série d'augmentations fixes sur plusieurs années jusqu'à ce qu'un objectif (souvent $15 ou plus) soit atteint.

segments.src: - **Indexing to inflation.** Once the target is reached, the wage rises each year based on a measure of price changes, usually a version of the Consumer Price Index (CPI). Some states cap the annual increase or pause it when the economy weakens.
segments.tr: - **Indexation sur l'inflation.** Une fois l'objectif atteint, le salaire augmente chaque année sur la base d'une mesure des variations de prix, généralement une version de l'Indice des Prix à la Consommation (IPC). Certains États plafonnent l'augmentation annuelle ou la suspendent lorsque l'économie ralentit.

segments.src: ## Where pay floors are rising
segments.tr: ## Où les planchers salariaux augmentent

segments.src: While the final numbers vary, the pattern is consistent from year to year.
segments.tr: Bien que les chiffres finaux varient, la tendance est constante d'une année sur l'autre.

segments.src: **States that index to inflation each January.** Many states adjust their rate on January 1 using a formula tied to the CPI.
segments.tr: **États qui s'indexent sur l'inflation chaque 1er janvier.** De nombreux États ajustent leur taux le 1er janvier en utilisant une formule liée à l'IPC.

segments.src: This group commonly includes states such as Arizona, California, Colorado, Connecticut, Illinois (under its scheduled path), Maine, Michigan, Minnesota, Missouri, Montana, New Jersey, New Mexico, Ohio, South Dakota, Vermont, Virginia, and Washington, along with others that have adopted similar rules.
segments.tr: Ce groupe comprend généralement des États tels que l'Arizona, la Californie, le Colorado, le Connecticut, l'Illinois (selon son parcours prévu), le Maine, le Michigan, le Minnesota, le Missouri, le Montana, le New Jersey, le Nouveau-Mexique, l'Ohio, le Dakota du Sud, le Vermont, la Virginie et Washington, ainsi que d'autres qui ont adopté des règles similaires.

segments.src: Washington has had one of the highest state minimum wages in the country, and California's rate is also well above the federal level.
segments.tr: Washington a eu l'un des salaires minimums d'État les plus élevés du pays, et le taux de la Californie est également bien supérieur au niveau fédéral.

segments.src: **States with scheduled steps.** Some states are still moving toward a target.
segments.tr: **États avec des augmentations progressives prévues.** Certains États progressent encore vers un objectif.

segments.src: Florida, for example, has a voter-approved schedule of annual raises, though its adjustments take effect in the fall rather than in January.
segments.tr: La Floride, par exemple, a un calendrier d'augmentations annuelles approuvé par les électeurs, bien que ses ajustements prennent effet à l'automne plutôt qu'en janvier.

segments.src: Nebraska voters approved a schedule that leads to inflation indexing in later years.
segments.tr: Les électeurs du Nebraska ont approuvé un calendrier qui conduit à une indexation sur l'inflation dans les années suivantes.

segments.src: New York has set indexing for upstate and downstate regions, with its own timeline.
segments.tr: New York a fixé une indexation pour les régions du nord et du sud de l'État, avec son propre calendrier.

segments.src: **Cities and counties.** Local governments often go further than their states, where state law allows.
segments.tr: **Villes et comtés.** Les gouvernements locaux vont souvent plus loin que leurs États, lorsque la loi de l'État le permet.

segments.src: Seattle, San Francisco, Los Angeles, Denver, Chicago, and many communities in the Washington, D.C.
segments.tr: Seattle, San Francisco, Los Angeles, Denver, Chicago et de nombreuses communautés de la région de Washington D.C.

segments.src: region adjust rates on January 1 or July 1, depending on local rules.
segments.tr: ajustent les taux le 1er janvier ou le 1er juillet, selon les règles locales.

segments.src: Some cities set higher rates for larger employers than for small ones, or for specific industries such as hotels or health care.
segments.tr: Certaines villes fixent des taux plus élevés pour les grands employeurs que pour les petits, ou pour des secteurs spécifiques tels que l'hôtellerie ou les soins de santé.

segments.src: **States with different schedules.** Not everyone changes in January.
segments.tr: **États avec des calendriers différents.** Tout le monde ne change pas en janvier.

segments.src: Oregon and the District of Columbia typically adjust on July 1, and a few other jurisdictions use other dates.
segments.tr: L'Oregon et le district de Columbia s'ajustent généralement le 1er juillet, et quelques autres juridictions utilisent d'autres dates.

segments.src: That is why it is important to check the effective date, not only the dollar amount.
segments.tr: C'est pourquoi il est important de vérifier la date d'entrée en vigueur, et pas seulement le montant en dollars.

segments.src: ## What drives the increases
segments.tr: ## Ce qui motive les augmentations

segments.src: Several factors explain why wage floors keep moving:
segments.tr: Plusieurs facteurs expliquent pourquoi les planchers salariaux continuent d'évoluer :

segments.src: 1. **Inflation.** When prices for housing, food, and transportation rise, indexing helps a minimum-wage paycheck keep up.
segments.tr: 1. **L'inflation.** Lorsque les prix du logement, de l'alimentation et du transport augmentent, l'indexation aide un chèque de paie au salaire minimum à suivre le rythme.

segments.src: 2. **Ballot measures and legislation.** Voters in several states have approved increases directly, and legislatures have passed multi-year schedules.
segments.tr: 2. **Initiatives électorales et législation.** Les électeurs de plusieurs États ont approuvé des augmentations directement, et les législatures ont voté des calendriers pluriannuels.

segments.src: 3. **Tight labor markets.** In many regions, employers already pay above the minimum to attract workers, which can make legal increases easier to absorb.
segments.tr: 3. **Marchés du travail tendus.** Dans de nombreuses régions, les employeurs paient déjà au-dessus du minimum pour attirer des travailleurs, ce qui peut rendre les augmentations légales plus faciles à absorber.

segments.src: 4. **Regional cost of living.** High-cost metro areas often adopt higher local minimums than the rest of their state.
segments.tr: 4. **Coût de la vie régional.** Les zones métropolitaines à coût élevé adoptent souvent des minimums locaux plus élevés que le reste de leur État.

segments.src: ## What it means for workers
segments.tr: ## Ce que cela signifie pour les travailleurs

segments.src: For a full-time worker, even a modest hourly increase adds up.
segments.tr: Pour un travailleur à temps plein, même une modeste augmentation horaire s'accumule.

segments.src: A raise of 30 to 60 cents an hour equals roughly $600 to $1,250 more per year for someone working 2,080 hours.
segments.tr: Une augmentation de 30 à 60 cents par heure équivaut à environ $600 à $1,250 de plus par an pour quelqu'un travaillant 2,080 heures.

segments.src: Workers in food service, retail, home care, and hospitality are most likely to be affected.
segments.tr: Les travailleurs de la restauration, du commerce de détail, des soins à domicile et de l'hôtellerie sont les plus susceptibles d'être touchés.

segments.src: Other points workers should know:
segments.tr: Autres points que les travailleurs devraient connaître :

segments.src: - **Tipped workers.** Rules differ widely. Some states require the full minimum wage before tips, while others allow employers to pay a lower cash wage if tips make up the difference.
segments.tr: - **Travailleurs au pourboire.** Les règles varient considérablement. Certains États exigent le salaire minimum complet avant les pourboires, tandis que d'autres permettent aux employeurs de payer un salaire en espèces inférieur si les pourboires comblent la différence.

segments.src: - **Overtime thresholds.** In some states, the salary level that exempts employees from overtime is tied to the minimum wage, so it can rise as well.
segments.tr: - **Seuils d'heures supplémentaires.** Dans certains États, le niveau de salaire qui exempte les employés des heures supplémentaires est lié au salaire minimum, il peut donc également augmenter.

segments.src: - **Posters and notices.** Employers are generally required to post the updated rate. If your paycheck does not reflect a new rate, you can contact your state labor agency.
segments.tr: - **Affiches et avis.** Les employeurs sont généralement tenus d'afficher le taux mis à jour. Si votre chèque de paie ne reflète pas un nouveau taux, vous pouvez contacter l'agence du travail de votre État.

segments.src: ## What it means for small businesses
segments.tr: ## Ce que cela signifie pour les petites entreprises

segments.src: Small employers feel these changes most directly, since labor is often their largest cost.
segments.tr: Les petits employeurs ressentent ces changements de la manière la plus directe, la main-d'œuvre étant souvent leur coût le plus important.

segments.src: Common responses include:
segments.tr: Les réponses courantes incluent :

segments.src: - **Updating payroll early.** Adjusting systems before January 1 avoids back-pay problems.
segments.tr: - **Mise à jour anticipée de la paie.** Ajuster les systèmes avant le 1er janvier évite les problèmes de rappels de salaire.

segments.src: - **Reviewing pricing and scheduling.** Some businesses adjust menu or service prices modestly, or fine-tune staffing during slower hours.
segments.tr: - **Examen des prix et des horaires.** Certaines entreprises ajustent modestement les prix des menus ou des services, ou affinent la dotation en personnel pendant les heures plus creuses.

segments.src: - **Watching the ripple effect.** When the entry-level wage goes up, employers often need to raise pay for experienced staff to keep pay differences fair.
segments.tr: - **Surveillance de l'effet d'entraînement.** Lorsque le salaire d'entrée augmente, les employeurs doivent souvent augmenter la rémunération du personnel expérimenté pour maintenir des différences de salaire équitables.

segments.src: - **Planning around predictable increases.** Indexing has one advantage for businesses: the formula is public, so increases are easier to forecast than sudden legislative changes.
segments.tr: - **Planification autour des augmentations prévisibles.** L'indexation présente un avantage pour les entreprises : la formule est publique, les augmentations sont donc plus faciles à prévoir que les changements législatifs soudains.

segments.src: Economists continue to debate the effects.
segments.tr: Les économistes continuent de débattre des effets.

segments.src: Some studies find small or no job losses from moderate increases, while others find reduced hours or slower hiring, particularly for small employers in lower-wage regions.
segments.tr: Certaines études constatent des pertes d'emplois faibles ou nulles suite à des augmentations modérées, tandis que d'autres constatent une réduction des heures ou un ralentissement des embauches, en particulier pour les petits employeurs dans les régions à bas salaires.

segments.src: Results often depend on how large the increase is relative to local wages.
segments.tr: Les résultats dépendent souvent de l'importance de l'augmentation par rapport aux salaires locaux.

segments.src: ## A quick checklist before January 1
segments.tr: ## Une liste de contrôle rapide avant le 1er janvier

segments.src: - Find the official 2027 rate for your state, county, and city.
segments.tr: - Trouvez le taux officiel pour 2027 de votre État, comté et ville.

segments.src: - Check whether your employer size or industry has a different rate.
segments.tr: - Vérifiez si la taille de votre employeur ou votre secteur d'activité applique un taux différent.

segments.src: - Confirm the effective date and any tipped-wage rules.
segments.tr: - Confirmez la date d'entrée en vigueur et toutes les règles relatives aux pourboires.

segments.src: - Employers: update payroll software, postings, and budgets.
segments.tr: - Employeurs : mettez à jour le logiciel de paie, les affichages et les budgets.

segments.src: - Workers: compare your first January paycheck with the new rate.
segments.tr: - Travailleurs : comparez votre premier chèque de paie de janvier avec le nouveau taux.

segments.src: ## The bottom line
segments.tr: ## En résumé

segments.src: With federal law unchanged for many years, the January 1 wage adjustment has become a regular feature of the American economy.
segments.tr: La loi fédérale étant inchangée depuis de nombreuses années, l'ajustement salarial du 1er janvier est devenu une caractéristique régulière de l'économie américaine.

segments.src: For workers it is a predictable boost, and for small businesses it is a planning task that benefits from early preparation.
segments.tr: Pour les travailleurs, c'est un coup de pouce prévisible, et pour les petites entreprises, c'est une tâche de planification qui bénéficie d'une préparation précoce.

segments.src: - **Reviewing pricing and scheduling.** Some businesses adjust menu or service prices modestly, or fine-tune staffing during slower hours.
segments.tr: - **Revisar preços e horários.** Algumas empresas ajustam modestamente os preços do menu ou dos serviços, ou aprimoram a escala de funcionários nos horários de menor movimento.

segments.src: - **Watching the ripple effect.** When the entry-level wage goes up, employers often need to raise pay for experienced staff to keep pay differences fair.

in.title: Kenaikan Gaji pada 1 Januari: Negara Bagian dan Kota Mana yang Menaikkan Upah Minimum untuk 2027

segments.src: Every year, millions of American workers see a slightly bigger paycheck on the first day of January, and they do not have to ask for it.
segments.tr: Setiap tahun, jutaan pekerja Amerika melihat gaji mereka sedikit lebih besar pada hari pertama bulan Januari, dan mereka tidak perlu memintanya.

segments.src: In a growing number of states and cities, the minimum wage rises automatically at the start of the year.
segments.tr: Di semakin banyak negara bagian dan kota, upah minimum naik secara otomatis pada awal tahun.

segments.src: Here is how those increases work, where they tend to happen, and what they mean for workers and small employers.
segments.tr: Berikut adalah cara kerja kenaikan tersebut, di mana kenaikan itu cenderung terjadi, dan apa artinya bagi pekerja serta pemberi kerja skala kecil.

segments.src: *Note: Exact 2027 rates are typically announced by state agencies in the fall.
segments.tr: *Catatan: Tarif resmi 2027 biasanya diumumkan oleh badan negara bagian pada musim gugur.

segments.src: Always confirm the final figure with your state or city labor department before making payroll or budgeting decisions.*
segments.tr: Selalu konfirmasikan angka akhir dengan departemen tenaga kerja negara bagian atau kota Anda sebelum membuat keputusan penggajian atau penganggaran.*

segments.src: ## Why do so many wages change on January 1?
segments.tr: ## Mengapa begitu banyak upah berubah pada 1 Januari?

segments.src: The federal minimum wage has been $7.25 an hour since 2009, and Congress has not changed it since.
segments.tr: Upah minimum federal telah berada di angka $7.25 per jam sejak 2009, dan Kongres belum mengubahnya sejak saat itu.

segments.src: Because of that, much of the action has moved to the states and local governments.
segments.tr: Karena itu, sebagian besar tindakan telah beralih ke negara bagian dan pemerintah daerah.

segments.src: Roughly thirty states and the District of Columbia set a minimum above the federal level, and many of them have built automatic adjustments into law so that lawmakers do not need to vote every year.
segments.tr: Sekitar tiga puluh negara bagian dan District of Columbia menetapkan upah minimum di atas tingkat federal, dan banyak dari mereka telah memasukkan penyesuaian otomatis ke dalam undang-undang sehingga pembuat kebijakan tidak perlu melakukan pemungutan suara setiap tahun.

segments.src: There are two common approaches:
segments.tr: Ada dua pendekatan umum:

segments.src: - **Scheduled step increases.** A law sets a path, such as a series of fixed raises over several years until a target (often $15 or more) is reached.
segments.tr: - **Kenaikan bertahap yang dijadwalkan.** Undang-undang menetapkan jalur, seperti serangkaian kenaikan tetap selama beberapa tahun hingga target (seringkali $15 atau lebih) tercapai.

segments.src: - **Indexing to inflation.** Once the target is reached, the wage rises each year based on a measure of price changes, usually a version of the Consumer Price Index (CPI). Some states cap the annual increase or pause it when the economy weakens.
segments.tr: - **Pengindeksan terhadap inflasi.** Setelah target tercapai, upah naik setiap tahun berdasarkan ukuran perubahan harga, biasanya versi dari Indeks Harga Konsumen (CPI). Beberapa negara bagian membatasi kenaikan tahunan atau menghentikannya sementara ketika ekonomi melemah.

segments.src: ## Where pay floors are rising
segments.tr: ## Di mana batas bawah upah meningkat

segments.src: While the final numbers vary, the pattern is consistent from year to year.
segments.tr: Meskipun angka akhirnya bervariasi, polanya konsisten dari tahun ke tahun.

segments.src: **States that index to inflation each January.** Many states adjust their rate on January 1 using a formula tied to the CPI.
segments.tr: **Negara bagian yang mengindeks terhadap inflasi setiap Januari.** Banyak negara bagian menyesuaikan tarif mereka pada 1 Januari menggunakan rumus yang terikat pada CPI.

segments.src: This group commonly includes states such as Arizona, California, Colorado, Connecticut, Illinois (under its scheduled path), Maine, Michigan, Minnesota, Missouri, Montana, New Jersey, New Mexico, Ohio, South Dakota, Vermont, Virginia, and Washington, along with others that have adopted similar rules.
segments.tr: Kelompok ini biasanya mencakup negara bagian seperti Arizona, California, Colorado, Connecticut, Illinois (di bawah jalur yang dijadwalkan), Maine, Michigan, Minnesota, Missouri, Montana, New Jersey, New Mexico, Ohio, South Dakota, Vermont, Virginia, dan Washington, bersama dengan negara bagian lain yang telah mengadopsi aturan serupa.

segments.src: Washington has had one of the highest state minimum wages in the country, and California's rate is also well above the federal level.
segments.tr: Washington memiliki salah satu upah minimum negara bagian tertinggi di negara ini, dan tarif California juga jauh di atas tingkat federal.

segments.src: **States with scheduled steps.** Some states are still moving toward a target.
segments.tr: **Negara bagian dengan langkah-langkah terjadwal.** Beberapa negara bagian masih bergerak menuju target.

segments.src: Florida, for example, has a voter-approved schedule of annual raises, though its adjustments take effect in the fall rather than in January.
segments.tr: Florida, misalnya, memiliki jadwal kenaikan tahunan yang disetujui pemilih, meskipun penyesuaiannya berlaku pada musim gugur, bukan pada bulan Januari.

segments.src: Nebraska voters approved a schedule that leads to inflation indexing in later years.
segments.tr: Pemilih Nebraska menyetujui jadwal yang mengarah pada pengindeksan inflasi di tahun-tahun berikutnya.

segments.src: New York has set indexing for upstate and downstate regions, with its own timeline.
segments.tr: New York telah menetapkan pengindeksan untuk wilayah utara dan selatan negara bagian, dengan linimasa tersendiri.

segments.src: **Cities and counties.** Local governments often go further than their states, where state law allows.
segments.tr: **Kota dan wilayah (county).** Pemerintah daerah sering kali melangkah lebih jauh daripada negara bagian mereka, di mana undang-undang negara bagian mengizinkannya.

segments.src: Seattle, San Francisco, Los Angeles, Denver, Chicago, and many communities in the Washington, D.C.
segments.tr: Seattle, San Francisco, Los Angeles, Denver, Chicago, dan banyak komunitas di wilayah Washington, D.C.

segments.src: region adjust rates on January 1 or July 1, depending on local rules.
segments.tr: menyesuaikan tarif pada 1 Januari atau 1 Juli, tergantung pada aturan setempat.

segments.src: Some cities set higher rates for larger employers than for small ones, or for specific industries such as hotels or health care.
segments.tr: Beberapa kota menetapkan tarif yang lebih tinggi untuk pemberi kerja yang lebih besar daripada untuk yang kecil, atau untuk industri tertentu seperti hotel atau perawatan kesehatan.

segments.src: **States with different schedules.** Not everyone changes in January.
segments.tr: **Negara bagian dengan jadwal berbeda.** Tidak semua orang berubah pada bulan Januari.

segments.src: Oregon and the District of Columbia typically adjust on July 1, and a few other jurisdictions use other dates.
segments.tr: Oregon dan District of Columbia biasanya menyesuaikan pada 1 Juli, dan beberapa yurisdiksi lain menggunakan tanggal lain.

segments.src: That is why it is important to check the effective date, not only the dollar amount.
segments.tr: Itulah mengapa penting untuk memeriksa tanggal efektif, bukan hanya jumlah dolarnya.

segments.src: ## What drives the increases
segments.tr: ## Apa yang mendorong kenaikan tersebut

segments.src: Several factors explain why wage floors keep moving:
segments.tr: Beberapa faktor menjelaskan mengapa batas bawah upah terus bergerak:

segments.src: 1. **Inflation.** When prices for housing, food, and transportation rise, indexing helps a minimum-wage paycheck keep up.
segments.tr: 1. **Inflasi.** Ketika harga untuk perumahan, makanan, dan transportasi naik, pengindeksan membantu gaji upah minimum untuk tetap mengikuti.

segments.src: 2. **Ballot measures and legislation.** Voters in several states have approved increases directly, and legislatures have passed multi-year schedules.
segments.tr: 2. **Langkah pemungutan suara dan legislasi.** Pemilih di beberapa negara bagian telah menyetujui kenaikan secara langsung, dan badan legislatif telah mengesahkan jadwal multi-tahun.

segments.src: 3. **Tight labor markets.** In many regions, employers already pay above the minimum to attract workers, which can make legal increases easier to absorb.
segments.tr: 3. **Pasar tenaga kerja yang ketat.** Di banyak wilayah, pemberi kerja sudah membayar di atas minimum untuk menarik pekerja, yang dapat membuat kenaikan legal lebih mudah diserap.

segments.src: 4. **Regional cost of living.** High-cost metro areas often adopt higher local minimums than the rest of their state.
segments.tr: 4. **Biaya hidup regional.** Wilayah metropolitan dengan biaya tinggi sering kali mengadopsi minimum lokal yang lebih tinggi daripada wilayah lain di negara bagian mereka.

segments.src: ## What it means for workers
segments.tr: ## Apa artinya bagi pekerja

segments.src: For a full-time worker, even a modest hourly increase adds up.
segments.tr: Bagi pekerja penuh waktu, kenaikan per jam yang sederhana pun akan terasa.

segments.src: A raise of 30 to 60 cents an hour equals roughly $600 to $1,250 more per year for someone working 2,080 hours.
segments.tr: Kenaikan 30 hingga 60 sen per jam setara dengan sekitar $600 hingga $1,250 lebih banyak per tahun bagi seseorang yang bekerja 2,080 jam.

segments.src: Workers in food service, retail, home care, and hospitality are most likely to be affected.
segments.tr: Pekerja di layanan makanan, ritel, perawatan di rumah, dan perhotelan adalah yang paling mungkin terpengaruh.

segments.src: Other points workers should know:
segments.tr: Poin lain yang harus diketahui pekerja:

segments.src: - **Tipped workers.** Rules differ widely. Some states require the full minimum wage before tips, while others allow employers to pay a lower cash wage if tips make up the difference.
segments.tr: - **Pekerja yang menerima tip.** Aturan sangat berbeda. Beberapa negara bagian mewajibkan upah minimum penuh sebelum tip, sementara yang lain mengizinkan pemberi kerja untuk membayar upah tunai yang lebih rendah jika tip menutupi selisihnya.

segments.src: - **Overtime thresholds.** In some states, the salary level that exempts employees from overtime is tied to the minimum wage, so it can rise as well.
segments.tr: - **Ambang batas lembur.** Di beberapa negara bagian, tingkat gaji yang membebaskan karyawan dari lembur terikat pada upah minimum, sehingga bisa naik juga.

segments.src: - **Posters and notices.** Employers are generally required to post the updated rate. If your paycheck does not reflect a new rate, you can contact your state labor agency.
segments.tr: - **Poster dan pemberitahuan.** Pemberi kerja umumnya diwajibkan untuk memasang tarif yang diperbarui. Jika gaji Anda tidak mencerminkan tarif baru, Anda dapat menghubungi badan tenaga kerja negara bagian Anda.

segments.src: ## What it means for small businesses
segments.tr: ## Apa artinya bagi bisnis kecil

segments.src: Small employers feel these changes most directly, since labor is often their largest cost.
segments.tr: Pemberi kerja skala kecil merasakan perubahan ini secara paling langsung, karena tenaga kerja sering kali menjadi biaya terbesar mereka.

segments.src: Common responses include:
segments.tr: Tanggapan umum meliputi:

segments.src: - **Updating payroll early.** Adjusting systems before January 1 avoids back-pay problems.
segments.tr: - **Memperbarui penggajian lebih awal.** Menyesuaikan sistem sebelum 1 Januari menghindari masalah pembayaran susulan.

segments.src: - **Reviewing pricing and scheduling.** Some businesses adjust menu or service prices modestly, or fine-tune staffing during slower hours.
segments.tr: - **Meninjau harga dan penjadwalan.** Beberapa bisnis menyesuaikan harga menu atau layanan secara sederhana, atau menyesuaikan staf selama jam-jam yang lebih sepi.

segments.src: - **Watching the ripple effect.** When the entry-level wage goes up, employers often need to raise pay for experienced staff to keep pay differences fair.
segments.tr: - **Mengamati efek riak.** Ketika upah tingkat awal naik, pemberi kerja sering kali perlu menaikkan gaji bagi staf berpengalaman agar perbedaan gaji tetap adil.

segments.src: - **Planning around predictable increases.** Indexing has one advantage for businesses: the formula is public, so increases are easier to forecast than sudden legislative changes.
segments.tr: - **Merencanakan kenaikan yang dapat diprediksi.** Pengindeksan memiliki satu keuntungan bagi bisnis: rumusnya bersifat publik, sehingga kenaikan lebih mudah diprediksi daripada perubahan legislatif yang tiba-tiba.

segments.src: Economists continue to debate the effects.
segments.tr: Para ekonom terus memperdebatkan efeknya.

segments.src: Some studies find small or no job losses from moderate increases, while others find reduced hours or slower hiring, particularly for small employers in lower-wage regions.
segments.tr: Beberapa studi menemukan kehilangan pekerjaan yang kecil atau tidak ada sama sekali dari kenaikan moderat, sementara yang lain menemukan pengurangan jam kerja atau perekrutan yang lebih lambat, terutama bagi pemberi kerja kecil di wilayah dengan upah lebih rendah.

segments.src: Results often depend on how large the increase is relative to local wages.
segments.tr: Hasil sering kali bergantung pada seberapa besar kenaikan tersebut relatif terhadap upah lokal.

segments.src: ## A quick checklist before January 1
segments.tr: ## Daftar periksa cepat sebelum 1 Januari

segments.src: - Find the official 2027 rate for your state, county, and city.
segments.tr: - Temukan tarif resmi 2027 untuk negara bagian, wilayah (county), dan kota Anda.

segments.src: - Check whether your employer size or industry has a different rate.
segments.tr: - Periksa apakah ukuran pemberi kerja atau industri Anda memiliki tarif yang berbeda.

segments.src: - Confirm the effective date and any tipped-wage rules.
segments.tr: - Konfirmasikan tanggal efektif dan aturan upah tip apa pun.

segments.src: - Employers: update payroll software, postings, and budgets.
segments.tr: - Pemberi kerja: perbarui perangkat lunak penggajian, poster, dan anggaran.

segments.src: - Workers: compare your first January paycheck with the new rate.
segments.tr: - Pekerja: bandingkan gaji Januari pertama Anda dengan tarif baru.

segments.src: ## The bottom line
segments.tr: ## Intinya

segments.src: With federal law unchanged for many years, the January 1 wage adjustment has become a regular feature of the American economy.
segments.tr: Dengan undang-undang federal yang tidak berubah selama bertahun-tahun, penyesuaian upah 1 Januari telah menjadi fitur reguler ekonomi Amerika.

segments.src: For workers it is a predictable boost, and for small businesses it is a planning task that benefits from early preparation.
segments.tr: Bagi pekerja, ini adalah dorongan yang dapat diprediksi, dan bagi bisnis kecil, ini adalah tugas perencanaan yang mendapat manfaat dari persiapan awal.

segments.src: Check your local rate from an official source, because the right number depends on where you work.
segments.tr: Periksa tarif lokal Anda dari sumber resmi, karena angka yang tepat bergantung pada tempat Anda bekerja.

segments.src: ## What drives the increases
segments.tr: ## 引き上げを推進する要因

segments.src: Several factors explain why wage floors keep moving:
segments.tr: 賃金の下限が動き続ける理由には、いくつかの要因があります：

segments.src: 1. **Inflation.** When prices for housing, food, and transportation rise, indexing helps a minimum-wage paycheck keep up.
segments.tr: 1. **インフレ。** 住宅、食料、交通費の価格が上昇すると、インフレ連動によって最低賃金の給与がそれに追随するのを助けます。

segments.src: 2. **Ballot measures and legislation.** Voters in several states have approved increases directly, and legislatures have passed multi-year schedules.
segments.tr: 2. **住民投票と立法。** いくつかの州の有権者が直接引き上げを承認し、議会が複数年のスケジュールを可決しました。

segments.src: 3. **Tight labor markets.** In many regions, employers already pay above the minimum to attract workers, which can make legal increases easier to absorb.
segments.tr: 3. **逼迫した労働市場。** 多くの地域で、雇用主は労働者を引き付けるためにすでに最低賃金を超える給与を支払っており、これにより法的な引き上げをより容易に吸収できるようになります。

segments.src: 4. **Regional cost of living.** High-cost metro areas often adopt higher local minimums than the rest of their state.
segments.tr: 4. **地域の生活費。** コストの高い都市圏では、多くの場合、州の他の地域よりも高い地域の最低賃金が採用されます。

segments.src: ## What it means for workers
segments.tr: ## 労働者にとっての意味

segments.src: For a full-time worker, even a modest hourly increase adds up.
segments.tr: フルタイムの労働者にとって、たとえわずかな時間給の引き上げであっても積み重なります。

segments.src: A raise of 30 to 60 cents an hour equals roughly $600 to $1,250 more per year for someone working 2,080 hours.
segments.tr: 1時間に30〜60セントの昇給は、2,080時間働く人にとって年間約$600〜$1,250の増加に相当します。

segments.src: Workers in food service, retail, home care, and hospitality are most likely to be affected.
segments.tr: フードサービス、小売、ホームケア、ホスピタリティ分野の労働者が最も影響を受ける可能性が高くなります。

segments.src: Other points workers should know:
segments.tr: 労働者が知っておくべきその他のポイント：

segments.src: - **Tipped workers.** Rules differ widely. Some states require the full minimum wage before tips, while others allow employers to pay a lower cash wage if tips make up the difference.
segments.tr: - **チップを受け取る労働者。** 規則は大きく異なります。チップの前に全額の最低賃金を要求する州もあれば、チップで差額が埋まる場合は雇用主がより低い現金を支払うことを認める州もあります。

segments.src: - **Overtime thresholds.** In some states, the salary level that exempts employees from overtime is tied to the minimum wage, so it can rise as well.
segments.tr: - **残業の閾値。** 一部の州では、従業員を残業から免除する給与水準が最低賃金と結び付けられているため、同様に上昇する可能性があります。

segments.src: - **Posters and notices.** Employers are generally required to post the updated rate. If your paycheck does not reflect a new rate, you can contact your state labor agency.
segments.tr: - **ポスターと通知。** 雇用主は通常、更新された料率を掲示することが義務付けられています。給与に新しい料率が反映されていない場合は、州の労働機関に連絡することができます。

segments.src: ## What it means for small businesses
segments.tr: ## 小規模企業にとっての意味

segments.src: Small employers feel these changes most directly, since labor is often their largest cost.
segments.tr: 小規模事業者は、多くの場合人件費が最大のコストであるため、これらの変更を最も直接的に感じます。

segments.src: Common responses include:
segments.tr: 一般的な対応には次のようなものがあります：

segments.src: - **Updating payroll early.** Adjusting systems before January 1 avoids back-pay problems.
segments.tr: - **給与計算の早期更新。** 1月1日より前にシステムを調整することで、バックペイ（遡及賃金）の問題を回避します。

segments.src: - **Reviewing pricing and scheduling.** Some businesses adjust menu or service prices modestly, or fine-tune staffing during slower hours.
segments.tr: - **価格設定とスケジュールの見直し。** 一部の企業では、メニューやサービスの価格を控えめに調整したり、客足の少ない時間帯のスタッフ配置を微調整したりします。

segments.src: - **Watching the ripple effect.** When the entry-level wage goes up, employers often need to raise pay for experienced staff to keep pay differences fair.
segments.tr: - **波及効果の監視。** エントリーレベルの賃金が上がると、雇用主は賃金の格差を公平に保つために、経験豊富なスタッフの給与を引き上げる必要があることがよくあります。

segments.src: - **Planning around predictable increases.** Indexing has one advantage for businesses: the formula is public, so increases are easier to forecast than sudden legislative changes.
segments.tr: - **予測可能な引き上げに向けた計画。** インフレ連動には企業にとって1つの利点があります。計算式が公開されているため、突然の法改正よりも引き上げを予測しやすくなります。

segments.src: Economists continue to debate the effects.
segments.tr: 経済学者たちはその影響について議論を続けています。

segments.src: Some studies find small or no job losses from moderate increases, while others find reduced hours or slower hiring, particularly for small employers in lower-wage regions.
segments.tr: 適度な引き上げによる雇用への影響は小さいか、あるいは見られないとする研究がある一方で、特に低賃金地域の小規模事業者において、労働時間の短縮や採用の鈍化が見られるとする研究もあります。

segments.src: Results often depend on how large the increase is relative to local wages.
segments.tr: 結果は、地域の賃金と比較して引き上げ幅がどれほど大きいかによって異なることがよくあります。

de.title: Gehaltserhöhung am 1. Januar: Welche Bundesstaaten und Städte den Mindestlohn für 2027 anheben

segments.src: Every year, millions of American workers see a slightly bigger paycheck on the first day of January, and they do not have to ask for it.
segments.tr: Jedes Jahr erhalten Millionen amerikanischer Arbeitnehmer am ersten Januar einen etwas größeren Gehaltsscheck, und sie müssen nicht darum bitten.

segments.src: In a growing number of states and cities, the minimum wage rises automatically at the start of the year.
segments.tr: In einer wachsenden Zahl von Bundesstaaten und Städten steigt der Mindestlohn zu Jahresbeginn automatisch.

segments.src: Here is how those increases work, where they tend to happen, and what they mean for workers and small employers.
segments.tr: Hier erfahren Sie, wie diese Erhöhungen funktionieren, wo sie tendenziell stattfinden und was sie für Arbeitnehmer und Kleinbetriebe bedeuten.

segments.src: *Note: Exact 2027 rates are typically announced by state agencies in the fall.
segments.tr: *Hinweis: Die genauen Sätze für 2027 werden in der Regel im Herbst von den Landesbehörden bekannt gegeben.

segments.src: Always confirm the final figure with your state or city labor department before making payroll or budgeting decisions.*
segments.tr: Bestätigen Sie den endgültigen Wert immer bei der Arbeitsbehörde Ihres Staates oder Ihrer Stadt, bevor Sie Lohn- oder Budgetentscheidungen treffen.*

segments.src: ## Why do so many wages change on January 1?
segments.tr: ## Warum ändern sich so viele Löhne am 1. Januar?

segments.src: The federal minimum wage has been $7.25 an hour since 2009, and Congress has not changed it since.
segments.tr: Der bundesweite Mindestlohn liegt seit 2009 bei 7,25 Dollar pro Stunde, und der Kongress hat ihn seither nicht geändert.

segments.src: Because of that, much of the action has moved to the states and local governments.
segments.tr: Aus diesem Grund hat sich ein Großteil des Geschehens auf die Bundesstaaten und Kommunalverwaltungen verlagert.

segments.src: Roughly thirty states and the District of Columbia set a minimum above the federal level, and many of them have built automatic adjustments into law so that lawmakers do not need to vote every year.
segments.tr: Etwa dreißig Bundesstaaten und der District of Columbia legen einen Mindestlohn fest, der über dem Bundessatz liegt, und viele von ihnen haben automatische Anpassungen gesetzlich verankert, sodass die Gesetzgeber nicht jedes Jahr abstimmen müssen.

segments.src: There are two common approaches:
segments.tr: Es gibt zwei gängige Ansätze:

segments.src: - **Scheduled step increases.** A law sets a path, such as a series of fixed raises over several years until a target (often $15 or more) is reached.
segments.tr: - **Geplante Stufenerhöhungen.** Ein Gesetz legt einen Pfad fest, wie zum Beispiel eine Reihe fester Erhöhungen über mehrere Jahre, bis ein Ziel (oft 15 Dollar oder mehr) erreicht ist.

segments.src: - **Indexing to inflation.** Once the target is reached, the wage rises each year based on a measure of price changes, usually a version of the Consumer Price Index (CPI). Some states cap the annual increase or pause it when the economy weakens.
segments.tr: - **Indexierung an die Inflation.** Sobald das Ziel erreicht ist, steigt der Lohn jedes Jahr auf Basis eines Maßes für Preisänderungen, meist einer Version des Verbraucherpreisindexes (VPI). Einige Bundesstaaten deckeln die jährliche Erhöhung oder pausieren sie, wenn die Wirtschaft schwächelt.

segments.src: ## Where pay floors are rising
segments.tr: ## Wo die Lohnuntergrenzen steigen

segments.src: While the final numbers vary, the pattern is consistent from year to year.
segments.tr: Obwohl die endgültigen Zahlen variieren, ist das Muster von Jahr zu Jahr konstant.

segments.src: **States that index to inflation each January.** Many states adjust their rate on January 1 using a formula tied to the CPI.
segments.tr: **Bundesstaaten, die jeden Januar an die Inflation indexieren.** Viele Bundesstaaten passen ihren Satz am 1. Januar mithilfe einer an den VPI gekoppelten Formel an.

segments.src: This group commonly includes states such as Arizona, California, Colorado, Connecticut, Illinois (under its scheduled path), Maine, Michigan, Minnesota, Missouri, Montana, New Jersey, New Mexico, Ohio, South Dakota, Vermont, Virginia, and Washington, along with others that have adopted similar rules.
segments.tr: Zu dieser Gruppe gehören üblicherweise Staaten wie Arizona, Kalifornien, Colorado, Connecticut, Illinois (im Rahmen seines geplanten Pfades), Maine, Michigan, Minnesota, Missouri, Montana, New Jersey, New Mexico, Ohio, South Dakota, Vermont, Virginia und Washington sowie andere, die ähnliche Regeln übernommen haben.

segments.src: Washington has had one of the highest state minimum wages in the country, and California's rate is also well above the federal level.
segments.tr: Washington hat einen der höchsten bundesstaatlichen Mindestlöhne des Landes, und auch der Satz von Kalifornien liegt weit über dem Bundesschnitt.

segments.src: **States with scheduled steps.** Some states are still moving toward a target.
segments.tr: **Bundesstaaten mit geplanten Stufen.** Einige Bundesstaaten bewegen sich noch auf ein Ziel zu.

segments.src: Florida, for example, has a voter-approved schedule of annual raises, though its adjustments take effect in the fall rather than in January.
segments.tr: Florida zum Beispiel hat einen von den Wählern genehmigten Zeitplan für jährliche Erhöhungen, obwohl die Anpassungen dort eher im Herbst als im Januar wirksam werden.

segments.src: Nebraska voters approved a schedule that leads to inflation indexing in later years.
segments.tr: Die Wähler in Nebraska haben einen Zeitplan genehmigt, der in späteren Jahren zu einer Inflationsindexierung führt.

segments.src: New York has set indexing for upstate and downstate regions, with its own timeline.
segments.tr: New York hat eine Indexierung für die Regionen Upstate und Downstate mit einem eigenen Zeitplan festgelegt.

segments.src: **Cities and counties.** Local governments often go further than their states, where state law allows.
segments.tr: **Städte und Bezirke.** Kommunalverwaltungen gehen oft weiter als ihre Bundesstaaten, sofern das Landesrecht dies zulässt.

segments.src: region adjust rates on January 1 or July 1, depending on local rules.

segments.src: Some cities set higher rates for larger employers than for small ones, or for specific industries such as hotels or health care.
segments.tr: Einige Städte legen höhere Sätze für größere Arbeitgeber fest als für kleine oder für bestimmte Branchen wie Hotels oder das Gesundheitswesen.

segments.src: **States with different schedules.** Not everyone changes in January.

segments.src: ## What drives the increases

segments.src: Several factors explain why wage floors keep moving:
segments.tr: Mehrere Faktoren erklären, warum sich die Lohnuntergrenzen weiterbewegen:

segments.src: 1. **Inflation.** When prices for housing, food, and transportation rise, indexing helps a minimum-wage paycheck keep up.
segments.tr: 1. **Inflation.** Wenn die Preise für Wohnen, Lebensmittel und Transport steigen, hilft die Indexierung einem Mindestlohn-Gehaltsschreiben, Schritt zu halten.

segments.src: 2. **Ballot measures and legislation.** Voters in several states have approved increases directly, and legislatures have passed multi-year schedules.
segments.tr: 2. **Wahlkreisinitiativen und Gesetzgebung.** Wähler in mehreren Bundesstaaten haben Erhöhungen direkt genehmigt, und Parlamente haben mehrjährige Zeitpläne verabschiedet.

segments.src: 3. **Tight labor markets.** In many regions, employers already pay above the minimum to attract workers, which can make legal increases easier to absorb.
segments.tr: 3. **Angespannte Arbeitsmärkte.** In vielen Regionen zahlen Arbeitgeber bereits über dem Mindestlohn, um Arbeitskräfte anzuziehen, was gesetzliche Erhöhungen leichter verdaulich machen kann.

segments.src: ## What it means for workers

segments.tr: Arbeitnehmer im Gastgewerbe, im Einzelhandel, in der häuslichen Pflege und im Hotel- und Gaststättengewerbe sind am wahrscheinlichsten betroffen.

segments.src: Other points workers should know:

segments.src: ## What it means for small businesses

segments.src: Small employers feel these changes most directly, since labor is often their largest cost.
segments.tr: Kleinbetriebe spüren diese Änderungen am direktesten, da die Lohnkosten oft ihre größte Ausgabe sind.

segments.src: Common responses include:
segments.tr: Gängige Reaktionen umfassen:

segments.src: - **Updating payroll early.** Adjusting systems before January 1 avoids back-pay problems.
segments.tr: - **Frühzeitige Aktualisierung der Gehaltsabrechnung.** Die Anpassung der Systeme vor dem 1. Januar vermeidet Probleme bei Nachzahlungen.

segments.src: - **Reviewing pricing and scheduling.** Some businesses adjust menu or service prices modestly, or fine-tune staffing during slower hours.
segments.tr: - **Überprüfung von Preisgestaltung und Dienstplänen.** Einige Unternehmen passen Menü- oder Dienstleistungspreise moderat an oder optimieren die Personalbesetzung in schwächeren Stunden.

segments.src: - **Watching the ripple effect.** When the entry-level wage goes up, employers often need to raise pay for experienced staff to keep pay differences fair.

segments.src: - **Planning around predictable increases.** Indexing has one advantage for businesses: the formula is public, so increases are easier to forecast than sudden legislative changes.

vi.title: Tăng lương vào ngày 1 tháng 1: Những tiểu bang và thành phố nào đang nâng mức lương tối thiểu cho năm 2027

segments.src: Every year, millions of American workers see a slightly bigger paycheck on the first day of January, and they do not have to ask for it.
segments.tr: Mỗi năm, hàng triệu người lao động Mỹ nhận được khoản tiền lương lớn hơn một chút vào ngày đầu tiên của tháng 1, và họ không cần phải yêu cầu điều đó.

segments.src: In a growing number of states and cities, the minimum wage rises automatically at the start of the year.
segments.tr: Tại ngày càng nhiều tiểu bang và thành phố, mức lương tối thiểu tự động tăng vào đầu năm.

segments.src: Here is how those increases work, where they tend to happen, and what they mean for workers and small employers.
segments.tr: Dưới đây là cách thức hoạt động của những đợt tăng đó, nơi chúng thường diễn ra, và ý nghĩa của chúng đối với người lao động và các chủ sử dụng lao động nhỏ.

segments.src: *Note: Exact 2027 rates are typically announced by state agencies in the fall.
segments.tr: *Lưu ý: Các mức cụ thể cho năm 2027 thường được các cơ quan tiểu bang thông báo vào mùa thu.

segments.src: Always confirm the final figure with your state or city labor department before making payroll or budgeting decisions.*
segments.tr: Luôn xác nhận con số cuối cùng với sở lao động tiểu bang hoặc thành phố của bạn trước khi đưa ra quyết định về bảng lương hoặc ngân sách.*

segments.src: ## Why do so many wages change on January 1?
segments.tr: ## Tại sao rất nhiều mức lương thay đổi vào ngày 1 tháng 1?

segments.src: The federal minimum wage has been $7.25 an hour since 2009, and Congress has not changed it since.
segments.tr: Mức lương tối thiểu liên bang đã giữ nguyên ở mức $7.25 một giờ kể từ năm 2009, và Quốc hội đã không thay đổi nó kể từ đó.

segments.src: Because of that, much of the action has moved to the states and local governments.
segments.tr: Do đó, phần lớn các hoạt động đã chuyển sang các tiểu bang và chính quyền địa phương.

segments.src: Roughly thirty states and the District of Columbia set a minimum above the federal level, and many of them have built automatic adjustments into law so that lawmakers do not need to vote every year.
segments.tr: Khoảng ba mươi tiểu bang và thủ đô Washington, D.C. đặt mức tối thiểu cao hơn mức liên bang, và nhiều nơi trong số đó đã đưa các điều chỉnh tự động vào luật để các nhà lập pháp không cần phải bỏ phiếu hàng năm.

segments.src: There are two common approaches:
segments.tr: Có hai cách tiếp cận phổ biến:

segments.src: - **Scheduled step increases.** A law sets a path, such as a series of fixed raises over several years until a target (often $15 or more) is reached.
segments.tr: - **Tăng theo bậc định sẵn.** Một luật thiết lập lộ trình, chẳng hạn như một loạt các đợt tăng cố định trong vài năm cho đến khi đạt được mục tiêu (thường là $15 trở lên).

segments.src: - **Indexing to inflation.** Once the target is reached, the wage rises each year based on a measure of price changes, usually a version of the Consumer Price Index (CPI). Some states cap the annual increase or pause it when the economy weakens.
segments.tr: - **Gắn với lạm phát.** Khi đạt được mục tiêu, mức lương sẽ tăng lên mỗi năm dựa trên thước đo biến động giá cả, thường là một phiên bản của Chỉ số Giá Tiêu dùng (CPI). Một số tiểu bang giới hạn mức tăng hàng năm hoặc tạm dừng khi nền kinh tế suy yếu.

segments.src: ## Where pay floors are rising
segments.tr: ## Nơi các sàn lương đang tăng

segments.src: While the final numbers vary, the pattern is consistent from year to year.
segments.tr: Mặc dù các con số cuối cùng khác nhau, mô hình này vẫn nhất quán từ năm này sang năm khác.

segments.src: **States that index to inflation each January.** Many states adjust their rate on January 1 using a formula tied to the CPI.
segments.tr: **Các tiểu bang gắn mức lương với lạm phát vào tháng 1 hàng năm.** Nhiều tiểu bang điều chỉnh mức lương của họ vào ngày 1 tháng 1 bằng cách sử dụng một công thức gắn liền với CPI.

segments.src: This group commonly includes states such as Arizona, California, Colorado, Connecticut, Illinois (under its scheduled path), Maine, Michigan, Minnesota, Missouri, Montana, New Jersey, New Mexico, Ohio, South Dakota, Vermont, Virginia, and Washington, along with others that have adopted similar rules.
segments.tr: Nhóm này thường bao gồm các tiểu bang như Arizona, California, Colorado, Connecticut, Illinois (theo lộ trình đã định), Maine, Michigan, Minnesota, Missouri, Montana, New Jersey, New Mexico, Ohio, South Dakota, Vermont, Virginia, và Washington, cùng với những tiểu bang khác đã áp dụng các quy tắc tương tự.

segments.src: Washington has had one of the highest state minimum wages in the country, and California's rate is also well above the federal level.
segments.tr: Washington đã có một trong những mức lương tối thiểu cấp tiểu bang cao nhất cả nước, và mức của California cũng cao hơn đáng kể so với mức liên bang.

segments.src: **States with scheduled steps.** Some states are still moving toward a target.
segments.tr: **Các tiểu bang có các bậc tăng định sẵn.** Một số tiểu bang vẫn đang tiến tới một mục tiêu.

segments.src: Florida, for example, has a voter-approved schedule of annual raises, though its adjustments take effect in the fall rather than in January.
segments.tr: Florida, ví dụ, có lịch trình tăng lương hàng năm được cử tri thông qua, mặc dù các điều chỉnh của bang này có hiệu lực vào mùa thu thay vì tháng 1.

segments.src: Nebraska voters approved a schedule that leads to inflation indexing in later years.
segments.tr: Cử tri Nebraska đã phê duyệt một lộ trình dẫn đến việc gắn chỉ số lạm phát trong những năm sau đó.

segments.src: New York has set indexing for upstate and downstate regions, with its own timeline.
segments.tr: New York đã thiết lập việc gắn chỉ số cho các khu vực phía bắc và phía nam tiểu bang, với mốc thời gian riêng.

segments.src: **Cities and counties.** Local governments often go further than their states, where state law allows.
segments.tr: **Các thành phố và quận hạt.** Chính quyền địa phương thường đi xa hơn các tiểu bang của họ, nơi luật pháp tiểu bang cho phép.

segments.src: Seattle, San Francisco, Los Angeles, Denver, Chicago, and many communities in the Washington, D.C.
segments.tr: Seattle, San Francisco, Los Angeles, Denver, Chicago, và nhiều cộng đồng ở khu vực Washington, D.C.

segments.src: region adjust rates on January 1 or July 1, depending on local rules.
segments.tr: điều chỉnh mức lương vào ngày 1 tháng 1 hoặc ngày 1 tháng 7, tùy thuộc vào quy định địa phương.

segments.src: Some cities set higher rates for larger employers than for small ones, or for specific industries such as hotels or health care.
segments.tr: Một số thành phố đặt mức lương cao hơn cho các nhà tuyển dụng lớn hơn so với các nhà tuyển dụng nhỏ, hoặc cho các ngành công nghiệp cụ thể như khách sạn hoặc chăm sóc sức khỏe.

segments.src: **States with different schedules.** Not everyone changes in January.
segments.tr: **Các tiểu bang có lịch trình khác nhau.** Không phải mọi nơi đều thay đổi vào tháng 1.

segments.src: Oregon and the District of Columbia typically adjust on July 1, and a few other jurisdictions use other dates.
segments.tr: Oregon và thủ đô Washington, D.C. thường điều chỉnh vào ngày 1 tháng 7, và một số khu vực pháp lý khác sử dụng các ngày khác.

segments.src: That is why it is important to check the effective date, not only the dollar amount.
segments.tr: Đó là lý do tại sao việc kiểm tra ngày có hiệu lực là quan trọng, không chỉ riêng số tiền.

segments.src: ## What drives the increases
segments.tr: ## Những yếu tố thúc đẩy việc tăng lương

segments.src: Several factors explain why wage floors keep moving:
segments.tr: Một số yếu tố giải thích tại sao các sàn lương tiếp tục dịch chuyển:

segments.src: 1. **Inflation.** When prices for housing, food, and transportation rise, indexing helps a minimum-wage paycheck keep up.
segments.tr: 1. **Lạm phát.** Khi giá nhà ở, thực phẩm và giao thông tăng, việc gắn chỉ số giúp tiền lương tối thiểu theo kịp.

segments.src: 2. **Ballot measures and legislation.** Voters in several states have approved increases directly, and legislatures have passed multi-year schedules.
segments.tr: 2. **Các biện pháp trưng cầu dân ý và lập pháp.** Cử tri ở một số tiểu bang đã trực tiếp thông qua các đợt tăng, và các cơ quan lập pháp đã thông qua các lộ trình nhiều năm.

segments.src: 3. **Tight labor markets.** In many regions, employers already pay above the minimum to attract workers, which can make legal increases easier to absorb.
segments.tr: 3. **Thị trường lao động thắt chặt.** Ở nhiều khu vực, người sử dụng lao động đã trả lương cao hơn mức tối thiểu để thu hút công nhân, điều này có thể giúp việc tăng lương theo luật định dễ tiếp nhận hơn.

segments.src: 4. **Regional cost of living.** High-cost metro areas often adopt higher local minimums than the rest of their state.
segments.tr: 4. **Chi phí sinh hoạt khu vực.** Các khu vực đô thị có chi phí cao thường áp dụng mức lương tối thiểu địa phương cao hơn phần còn lại của tiểu bang.

segments.src: ## What it means for workers
segments.tr: ## Ý nghĩa đối với người lao động

segments.src: For a full-time worker, even a modest hourly increase adds up.
segments.tr: Đối với một nhân viên toàn thời gian, ngay cả một mức tăng theo giờ khiêm tốn cũng tích lũy thành một khoản đáng kể.

segments.src: A raise of 30 to 60 cents an hour equals roughly $600 to $1,250 more per year for someone working 2,080 hours.
segments.tr: Mức tăng từ 30 đến 60 xu một giờ tương đương với khoảng $600 đến $1,250 nhiều hơn mỗi năm đối với một người làm việc 2,080 giờ.

segments.src: Workers in food service, retail, home care, and hospitality are most likely to be affected.
segments.tr: Người lao động trong ngành dịch vụ ăn uống, bán lẻ, chăm sóc tại nhà và khách sạn có nhiều khả năng bị ảnh hưởng nhất.

segments.src: Other points workers should know:
segments.tr: Các điểm khác mà người lao động nên biết:

segments.src: - **Tipped workers.** Rules differ widely. Some states require the full minimum wage before tips, while others allow employers to pay a lower cash wage if tips make up the difference.
segments.tr: - **Nhân viên nhận tiền boa.** Các quy tắc khác nhau rất nhiều. Một số tiểu bang yêu cầu mức lương tối thiểu đầy đủ trước tiền boa, trong khi những tiểu bang khác cho phép người sử dụng lao động trả mức lương tiền mặt thấp hơn nếu tiền boa bù đắp vào phần chênh lệch.

segments.src: - **Overtime thresholds.** In some states, the salary level that exempts employees from overtime is tied to the minimum wage, so it can rise as well.
segments.tr: - **Ngưỡng làm thêm giờ.** Ở một số tiểu bang, mức lương miễn cho nhân viên làm thêm giờ được gắn liền với lương tối thiểu, vì vậy nó cũng có thể tăng lên.

segments.src: - **Posters and notices.** Employers are generally required to post the updated rate. If your paycheck does not reflect a new rate, you can contact your state labor agency.
segments.tr: - **Áp phích và thông báo.** Người sử dụng lao động thường bắt buộc phải đăng tải mức lương đã cập nhật. Nếu bảng lương của bạn không phản ánh mức mới, bạn có thể liên hệ với cơ quan lao động tiểu bang.

segments.src: ## What it means for small businesses
segments.tr: ## Ý nghĩa đối với các doanh nghiệp nhỏ

segments.src: Small employers feel these changes most directly, since labor is often their largest cost.
segments.tr: Các chủ sử dụng lao động nhỏ cảm nhận những thay đổi này một cách trực tiếp nhất, vì chi phí lao động thường là chi phí lớn nhất của họ.

segments.src: Common responses include:
segments.tr: Các phản ứng phổ biến bao gồm:

segments.src: - **Updating payroll early.** Adjusting systems before January 1 avoids back-pay problems.
segments.tr: - **Cập nhật bảng lương sớm.** Điều chỉnh hệ thống trước ngày 1 tháng 1 giúp tránh các vấn đề về trả lương bù.

segments.src: - **Reviewing pricing and scheduling.** Some businesses adjust menu or service prices modestly, or fine-tune staffing during slower hours.
segments.tr: - **Xem xét giá cả và lịch trình.** Một số doanh nghiệp điều chỉnh giá thực đơn hoặc dịch vụ một cách khiêm tốn, hoặc tinh chỉnh việc bố trí nhân sự trong những giờ ít khách hơn.

segments.src: - **Watching the ripple effect.** When the entry-level wage goes up, employers often need to raise pay for experienced staff to keep pay differences fair.
segments.tr: - **Theo dõi hiệu ứng lan tỏa.** Khi mức lương khởi điểm tăng lên, người sử dụng lao động thường cần phải tăng lương cho nhân viên có kinh nghiệm để giữ cho sự khác biệt về lương được công bằng.

segments.src: - **Planning around predictable increases.** Indexing has one advantage for businesses: the formula is public, so increases are easier to forecast than sudden legislative changes.
segments.tr: - **Lập kế hoạch xung quanh các khoản tăng có thể dự đoán được.** Việc gắn chỉ số có một lợi thế cho các doanh nghiệp: công thức là công khai, vì vậy việc tăng lương dễ dự đoán hơn so với những thay đổi lập pháp đột ngột.

segments.src: Economists continue to debate the effects.
segments.tr: Các nhà kinh tế tiếp tục tranh luận về các tác động.

segments.src: Some studies find small or no job losses from moderate increases, while others find reduced hours or slower hiring, particularly for small employers in lower-wage regions.
segments.tr: Một số nghiên cứu tìm thấy ít hoặc không có việc làm bị mất từ các mức tăng vừa phải, trong khi những nghiên cứu khác lại thấy giảm giờ làm hoặc tuyển dụng chậm hơn, đặc biệt là đối với các nhà tuyển dụng nhỏ ở các khu vực có mức lương thấp hơn.

segments.src: Results often depend on how large the increase is relative to local wages.
segments.tr: Kết quả thường phụ thuộc vào mức độ tăng lớn đến đâu so với mức lương địa phương.

segments.src: ## A quick checklist before January 1
segments.tr: ## Một danh sách kiểm tra nhanh trước ngày 1 tháng 1

segments.src: - Find the official 2027 rate for your state, county, and city.
segments.tr: - Tìm mức chính thức năm 2027 cho tiểu bang, quận và thành phố của bạn.

segments.src: - Check whether your employer size or industry has a different rate.
segments.tr: - Kiểm tra xem quy mô nhà tuyển dụng hoặc ngành nghề của bạn có mức lương khác hay không.

segments.src: - Confirm the effective date and any tipped-wage rules.
segments.tr: - Xác nhận ngày có hiệu lực và bất kỳ quy tắc lương boa nào.

segments.src: - Employers: update payroll software, postings, and budgets.
segments.tr: - Người sử dụng lao động: cập nhật phần mềm bảng lương, thông báo và ngân sách.

segments.src: - Workers: compare your first January paycheck with the new rate.
segments.tr: - Người lao động: so sánh bảng lương tháng 1 đầu tiên của bạn với mức lương mới.

segments.src: ## The bottom line
segments.tr: ## Điểm mấu chốt

segments.src: With federal law unchanged for many years, the January 1 wage adjustment has become a regular feature of the American economy.
segments.tr: Với luật liên bang không đổi trong nhiều năm, việc điều chỉnh lương ngày 1 tháng 1 đã trở thành một tính năng thường xuyên của nền kinh tế Mỹ.

segments.src: For workers it is a predictable boost, and for small businesses it is a planning task that benefits from early preparation.
segments.tr: Đối với người lao động, đó là một sự thúc đẩy có thể dự đoán được, và đối với các doanh nghiệp nhỏ, đó là một công việc lập kế hoạch được hưởng lợi từ việc chuẩn bị sớm.

segments.src: Check your local rate from an official source, because the right number depends on where you work.
segments.tr: Kiểm tra mức lương địa phương của bạn từ nguồn chính thống, bởi vì con số đúng phụ thuộc vào nơi bạn làm việc.
